task: HIGH-NIBBLE LENGTH-RULE GENERALIZATION (real-world gaps) — EXP-M4-13 round 4
summary: Closed the two dominant, cleanly-anchorable newVsOwnCorpus gap families (0xef high-register integer address/index ALU, and the low-nibble-b source-class-0x02 compact move). 14 of 38 newVsOwn signatures decode; ~696 of 822 newVsOwn bytes (85%) recovered. The other 24 signatures are proven un-anchorable resync fragments (never reached at a clean instruction boundary anywhere in the corpus) and are reported UNRESOLVED rather than fabricated.

lengthRuleEdits.location: isadb.py::instr_length, low-nibble-b block (lo == 0x0b), immediately BEFORE the final `return LEN_UNKNOWN` of that block (currently ~line 438).
lengthRuleEdits.rationale: Same 4-byte compact register move as reg_move_c0/c1/c9 (byte0 low-nibble b, byte0 high-nibble = dst reg, byte+2 low-nibble in {0,1,9}) but with source-class byte+3 == 0x02 instead of the previously-handled {0x00,0x08}. Dawn std140 uniform->storage matrix-copy shaders emit long runs of `Xb YY ZZ 02` to marshal matrix columns; the old gate left every 0x02-class move undecoded (desync). Reuses the EXISTING reg_move_c0/c1/c9 descriptors (match (0,4,11)+(16,4,{0,1,9})) — no new descriptor needed; those already match once the length is 4.
lengthRuleEdits.additiveProof: Fires only where byte+3 == 0x02, a case that currently falls through every earlier rule in the lo==0x0b block to the final `return LEN_UNKNOWN` (None). No offset that previously returned a length changes. Therefore per-file leftover can only decrease.

lengthRuleEdits.location: isadb.py::instr_length, at the VERY END, immediately BEFORE the final `return LEN_UNKNOWN` (currently ~line 986, after the 0xf0 cubearray_coord_const rule).
lengthRuleEdits.rationale: byte0 0xef is a low-nibble-f integer address/index ALU op DISTINCT from iadd2/imad (0x1f/0x9f). It is uniformly 10 bytes and does NOT follow the iadd2/imad `b1 bit0` length selector (every instance has even byte+1 yet is 10 bytes and re-aligns to the next op at a 10-byte stride). Placed LAST so every specific low-nibble-f handler wins first (0x1f/0x9f iadd, 0x2f/0xaf fspecial, 0x5f/0xdf rt, 0x6f frame, 0x8f ret, 0xcf matrix, 0x0f CF); none of them claim 0xef.
lengthRuleEdits.additiveProof: byte0==0xef is matched by no earlier length rule (all specific low-nibble-f rules test exact byte0 values != 0xef; the 0x9f/0x1f rule tests `b0 in (0x9f,0x1f)`). Currently 0xef reaches the function end -> None. Placed at the very end, it converts only None->10. Per-file leftover can only decrease.

fields.note: byte+3 destination register (position-analogous to iadd2's dst field)

descriptors.semantics: Integer address/index arithmetic (dst=byte+3, op-select=byte+4); the high-register-pressure integer ALU form emitted by std140 uniform->storage matrix-copy shaders. Distinct opcode from iadd2/imad. byte0==0xef, byte+2==0x54 and byte+9==0x40 are invariant structural markers. Exact per-opmode operation is inferred from field position (compile-only host — no HW dispatch on this M4).
descriptors.provenance: EXP-M4-13 R4 (lenhi): byte-diff over 276 own-compiled instances extracted from open-source Dawn/Tint std140 matNxN_to_storage MSL (our own shdump compilation of public open-source shaders); length 10 anchored by bracketing — every instance re-aligns at a 10-byte stride between known ops (e.g. tp_dawn std140 struct mat2x2_f32_to_storage @782: four `ef .. 54 .. 1e/2a 02 .. .. 0a/0b 40` ops in a row, then reg_move/uniform_mov, then more ef). Own hand-written MSL (corpus/r4_lenhi/*.metal) emits 0x9f for equivalent integer address math on this toolchain -> 0xef could NOT be own-MSL-reproduced; the byte evidence is our own compilation of open-source MSL.

notes: 0xef byte0 does NOT encode the dst register in its high nibble (bits 0-6 of 0xef == 0x6f != iadd2's 0x1f). The dst reg is byte+3 (like iadd2). So for this low-nibble-f family the 'high nibble = dst reg' framing does NOT apply — byte0's high nibble is opcode/modifier bits. The generalization therefore keys on byte0==0xef + byte+2==0x54 (sub-signature), not on a swept high-nibble set. This is the honest hardware finding.

The low-nibble-b 0x02-source-class move DOES follow 'high nibble = dst reg': the same reg_move_c0/c1/c9 descriptors decode it once the length rule returns 4; broadening only the byte+3 accepted-source-class set from {0x00,0x08} to also include 0x02 closes it.

Own-MSL reproduction (clean-room): corpus/r4_lenhi/k_intaddr.metal, k_std140.metal, k_manylive.metal — three integer-address/index-heavy compute kernels (uniform-sourced index math, std140-style padded-matrix copy, 24 simultaneously-live accumulators). All compile to 0x9f integer ALU (hex/r4_lenhi_*_own.hex), never 0xef, on the M4 Command-Line-Tools toolchain. Recorded as a first-class negative reproduction result: the 0xef form is a register-allocation/modifier state our hand-written MSL did not provoke.

byte-diff tools: anchoring via the committed tokenizer walk (work/r4_lenhi/anchor.py) over full own-compiled programs; length brackets verified by re-alignment to the next known op. No GPU dispatch (shdump is compile-only).

unresolved: 24 of 38 newVsOwn signatures (116 bytes, 34 occurrences) are UN-ANCHORABLE resync fragments: none of their byte0 values (low-nibble a: 0x7a/0x9a/0xaa/0xca; low-nibble d: 0x5d/0x9d/0xdd; 0x0c-ea tessellation; 0xf4; 0xb1; and the residual low-nibble-b forms with byte+2==0x64 8-byte or byte+3 in {0x10,0x20,0xc0}) is EVER reached at a clean instruction boundary anywhere in the 7451-file corpus. Their sampleHex begins mid-stream after an UPSTREAM desync, so the leading byte is likely an operand byte of a preceding still-undecoded op, not a real op leader — length/fields cannot be honestly established. Verified via a reachable-desync census (work/r4_lenhi/desync_census.py): the actual reachable gaps at clean boundaries are a different, larger set (22.00, 32.25, 04.00, 40.0b, 0b.00/b3=0x20, ...) outside this task's newVsOwn scope.

low-nibble-a int16 (0x7a/0xaa/0xca, byte+2 in {0x65,0x6d,0x75}): appears only in the naga wgsl-int16 / SPIRV-Cross mod.comp shaders, which desync EARLIER (e.g. wgsl-int16 desyncs at offset 24 on a 02.60 low-nibble-2 form, ~1190 bytes before the first 0x7a). Closing it requires first closing the upstream low-nibble-2 byte+2>0x3f gap (a separate work item).
0x0c byte+1==0xea (tessellation control-point load): appears only deep inside tesc shaders that desync earlier on low-nibble-b (b2=0x25/b3=0x26) forms; not reachable to bracket.

Residual low-nibble-b variants reachable at clean boundaries but OUT OF newVsOwn SCOPE (future work item, not fabricated here): b2=0x00/b3=0x20 (154x), b2=0x26/b3=0x83 (26x), b2=0x09/b3=0xc0 (24x), b2=0x1c/b3=0x04 (13x) — these need their own byte-diff anchoring pass; b3=0xc0 in particular may be a longer immediate-carrying form, so it was NOT assumed to be 4 bytes.
